title: Reuse copyStringToClipboard / ClipboardButton for clipboard writes instead of calling navigator.clipboard directly
answers: What's the right way to add a copy-to-clipboard button?
Should I call navigator.clipboard.writeText directly in a component?
Grafana convention for copy link / copy to clipboard UI
body:
Fix pattern / convention: for simple copy actions tied to a button, use @grafana/ui's ClipboardButton with a getText() callback instead of hand-rolling an <a>/<Button> with an onClick that calls navigator.clipboard.writeText — this was requested in review and replaced a custom anchor+Button+onClick implementation in ShareSpanButton.tsx. For copy actions not expressed as a ClipboardButton (e.g. a menu item), call the shared copyStringToClipboard(string) helper rather than navigator.clipboard.writeText directly, since it already encodes the ClipboardItem/isSecureContext/execCommand fallback chain.
Constraints: applies to any new copy-to-clipboard UI; if ClipboardButton can't be used (non-button context), always route through copyStringToClipboard rather than re-implementing the secure-context/feature-detection logic.
applies: Grafana frontend components adding or modifying copy-to-clipboard functionality

search: Clipboard write operations must route through either @grafana/ui's ClipboardButton with getText() callback for button-tied actions, or the copyStringToClipboard(string) helper for non-button contexts—do not call navigator.clipboard.writeText directly. The copyStringToClipboard function encodes the ClipboardItem, isSecureContext, and execCommand fallback chain, preventing reimplementation drift. Applies to any new or modified copy-to-clipboard UI functionality in Grafana frontend components, including menu items and other non-button copy surfaces.
